The wider cohort · online & network
Also applied · the wider pool

Kobe drew a broader health-and-longevity field than joined the residency. The density of these ventures around a biotech city is itself a signal for where Sanctuary sits.

Chloë
Co-hosts longevity events in Japan; came from Scrum.inc and has been living between the US and Japan.
Seaweed hydration jelly stick
A carrageenan recovery gel from MYCL, a biomaterials company replacing leather and plastic with seaweed, to test as a functional food after heat, onsen or training.
Hayat Longevity
A functional-longevity clinic that turns external lab reports into a proprietary longevity score, now aiming to license its system and app to clinics across Malaysia and Indonesia.
Stem-cell exosome therapy
A preclinical exosome nasal spray for cognitive decline and brain fog, exploring entry into Japan's regenerative-medicine ecosystem.
Wearable 3D motion capture
A multipoint clip-on sensor system that tracks posture and range of motion, moving from B2B analytics to a consumer fitness and strength-training device.
Home exercise device
A simple at-home device giving elderly users daily calf and quad targets with a rep counter, to hold lower-limb strength and independence.
Senior living community
Small independent homes with shared facilities and 24/7 care, designed so healthy seniors live actively alongside younger generations.
Feroce
An AI care companion that follows a clinic's care plan between visits, handling routine follow-up and bringing clinicians in only when needed.
One thesis, many angles02, The unifying thesis

Everyone works towards the same thesis

“
Every builder here is making a deeply human capability (intimacy, companionship, conversation, real demand, embodied craft) and testing one question: can AI scale the most human part of it without hollowing it out?
CARL · the act

Intimacy

Coaching men through sexual health, the part that never scaled because it was one-to-one and human. Can an AI hold that conversation?

ANNA · the inner life

Companionship

M8, an agent that reads affect signals in language and supports growth without mirroring you. The human interior, made legible to a machine.

ANKIT · the connection

Conversation

Compass, capturing and making sense of spoken conversation, building context around what people say.

JANE · the signal

Real demand

Finding genuine willingness to pay through ads and smoke tests, separating a human yes from a polite one.

ANDREJ · the craft

Embodied knowledge

Learning what of an embodied skill can be made transferable and remote.

THE HOUSE · the proof

Lived, not theorized

The thesis was tested on the street and at the table, magic, conversation, cooking, not only in the product.

Baseline → showcase04, Pre / post

What they set out to do, and what happened

Five builders have both a baseline from the onboarding call and a reported outcome, from the closing showcase or a follow-up call. The honest arc of each:

JaneGrant Finder · Black Dot AdsOnline
Baseline, onboarding
Work both the consultancy and the product-market fit she'd found; land a first sale that takes none of her own time in the moment.
Showcase, outcome
Rebuilt Grant Finder from an email list into a filterable grants database with movable paywalls and smoke tests. Readying another round of conversion ads. Still no external sale, but sustained organic signups she didn't pay for, a demand signal worth chasing. Next: apply for grants herself, using her own medicine.
Health  Bali gyms with office, food and recovery in one place made protein and training easy; the fascia-release and meditation goal slipped.
AnkitCompass → DLogosOnline
Baseline, onboarding
Launch Compass to the 80-person waitlist, gather testimonials and feedback, explore founder-community distribution, joining for accountability.
Showcase, outcome
By the showcase the energy had moved to DLogos, a two-sided podcasting marketplace between listeners and hosts, with a January launch and partners being lined up. Conviction shift: in an age where anything can be built, the defensible thing is relationships, product in service of them. Delegating across a growing team.
Collaboration  Worked closely with Anna, who joined DLogos on product and distribution, the cohort's clearest cross-collaboration.
AnnaM8 → DLogosOnline
Baseline, onboarding
Launch the web version of M8, a companion reading affect signals in chat to support growth without mirroring. Plus PhD AI research (TechnoGod).
Showcase, outcome
Shipped a prototype and joined Ankit's DLogos across product and social distribution, complementing the team where it needed it. Named the structural gap openly: less scaffolding this cohort than before left her unsure what to work on, which sharpened what next time needs.
Health  A hard stretch, travel and illness through San Francisco broke her sleep schedule; recovery deferred to a stable base in Thailand.
CarlSexual-health AI → bra company agentsIRL · Kobe
Baseline, onboarding
Build a pilot of the sexual-health AI agent and its knowledge base: the core infrastructure for a restart with a Japanese partner early next year.
Follow-up call, outcome
Did not finish the pilot, and put the sexual-health venture on ice. Two weeks of focus made him fluent with AI agents: which mode to use for which task, and how to make them check each other. He now applies this to his bra company, a running business he led for about 17 years. In one week he built a catalog agent with a large effect on the business. Next come a bra-fitting agent for the website and stores, a buying bot and a finance bot, to replace an admin layer that once cost about a million dollars a year.
The house  His first time in 20 years living with anyone outside his family. New people, places and work broke his routine and generated ideas. Andrej's questions had the most influence; Matt and Sho added new points of view.
AndrejSanctuary · the report · embodied craftIRL · host
Baseline, onboarding
Conclude Sanctuary start-to-finish; collaborate with Carl on the futures of sexual health; build prototypes; find the right structure for the report; test living with someone he'd never met.
Showcase, outcome
The live-with-a-stranger experiment worked, and became the design insight. Weighed Sanctuary's direction, a micro-VC with Kyle and Ramona vs. a permanent physical home with Matt, and leaned toward the physical space. Deliberately ran this edition looser to test the living dynamic.
Health  No alcohol, but a week of 3–4 hours' sleep, not sustainable, and a direct input to the stricter next-time guidelines.
The lead venture05, Carl's project

From a sexual-health pilot to an agent-run business

Carl came with twenty years of product businesses and a seven-year sexual-health venture that only worked one-to-one. The plan for Kobe was to build the AI pilot for that venture. After the residency he changed direction: the skills he built now go first into his bra company.

The plan, October

An AI coach for men's sexual health

A knowledge base that diagnoses, recommends resources and runs weekly check-ins, as the core of a restart with a Japanese partner early next year. The PMF workshop narrowed it to men 45–60 and one first prototype:

  • Intake quiz, with questions that become more personal step by step
  • Curated, science-backed knowledge base
  • Chatbot on that knowledge base
  • Personal 90-day roadmap
Now, November

Agents for his bra company

He put the sexual-health venture on ice and moved the skills to his bra company, a running business he led for about 17 years before his break.

  • A catalog agent, built in one week, already with a large effect on the business
  • A bra-fitting agent next, for the website and possibly the stores
  • Buying and finance bots after that
  • The goal: an agent-run admin layer that once took about a million dollars a year in staff and agencies

Sexual health stays his side quest. In his words, the time at Sanctuary “definitely wasn't wasted”: the residency built the skills, and they paid off first in a different business.

Forward06, Next edition

What we'd change

Design changes

More strangers, more structure

  • Invite more strangers through ads, widen beyond the known network
  • Deepen the membership-and-mentorship dynamic practised with Carl, so each cohort has a lead mentor
  • Bring back the check-in points the online cohort missed, structure the loop Anna named
Longevity guidelines

A stricter container

  • No alcohol
  • Red light in the evenings
  • Hold the shared gym and cooking baseline that worked
  • A co-organised party at the end, the closing ritual, planned together

The cohort thesis
Where value forms, why now, why us

Value forms where AI meets intimate human domains

Sexual health, emotional growth, care and conversation. In these domains the limit is trust, not technology.

  • Carl's coaching never scaled because it was one-to-one.
  • M8 reads affect without flattering its user.
  • Compass and DLogos keep the relationship at the centre.

The time is now

  • Models can finally carry an expert conversation.
  • People tell an AI what they would not tell a person.
  • Cheap building makes products easy to copy, so the defensible assets are domain knowledge, trust and relationships.

The group can get there first

It already holds the scarce inputs:

  • A sexual-health operator with seven years in the field, a Japanese partner and a first customer to win.
  • Research in affective neuroscience.
  • Founders who test products on each other.
  • A house where strangers live, cook and go out together, so intimate products meet real people before they meet a market.
  • A base in Kobe: an ageing, longevity-minded market around a biotech cluster.

The edge is still early

No project reported a paying customer at the showcase. The next cohort must turn access and trust into sales.
